Extract Questions, Answers and Cited Reports From a Word Document

Source: R/docx_qa.R
extract_docx_qa.Rd

Reads the body of a `.docx` that lists investigator questions, each followed by the answer paragraphs written for it, and returns one row per question with its answer and the report files the answer cites. This is for tracking reviewer or PI questions across a project (a Q&A sheet in Word turned into a deliverables table); it does not read Word's comments or who made a tracked change, for which see [docx_review_extract()].

Usage

extract_docx_qa(
  docx_path,
  question_pattern = "^(What|Why|How|Summarize|Explain|Can|Is|Are)\\b|\\?$",
  citation_pattern = "(?i)\\b[[:alnum:]_.\\-]+\\.(pdf|docx|html)\\b",
  index_data = NULL,
  index_file_col = "file",
  index_path_col = "path"
)

Arguments

docx_path

Path to the `.docx` file.

question_pattern

Regular expression (PCRE) that marks a question paragraph. The default matches paragraphs that begin with a question word (as a whole word, so "Isolated" is not "Is") or end with `?`.

citation_pattern

Regular expression (PCRE) for a cited file name. The default matches names ending in `.pdf`, `.docx` or `.html`, in any letter case.

index_data

Optional data frame of the deliverables, with one row per file.

index_file_col, index_path_col

Columns of `index_data` with the file name and with the path or URL the link should point to (default `"file"` and `"path"`).

Value

A tibble with one row per question: `question_id`, `question`, `answer`, `n_answer_paragraphs`, `citations` (list of character vectors), `citation_files` (the citations joined with `"; "`) and, when `index_data` is given, `links` (list of HYPERLINK formulas, one per resolved citation) and `unresolved_citations` (joined with `"; "`).

Details

A paragraph is a **question** if it matches `question_pattern`; every following paragraph up to the next question is part of its **answer** (joined with a line break). Paragraphs before the first question are ignored. The text is what the document currently reads: tracked insertions count, tracked deletions do not. A table's paragraphs count, in document order; the text of a text box is read once, as its own paragraph. Empty paragraphs are dropped.

**The default `question_pattern` is simple and can misfire**: an answer paragraph that begins with one of its words ("Can't say.", "How we handled it: see a.pdf") or ends with `?` is taken for a new question, and the answer it interrupts is cut short without a warning. Check `n_answer_paragraphs`, or give a stricter pattern (for example `"^Q[0-9]+[.:]"` when the questions are numbered).

**Citations** are the matches of `citation_pattern` in the answer. With `index_data`, each is looked up (by file name, ignoring case and folders) in the index; the column `links` then holds, per question, the Excel formulas `=HYPERLINK("<path>", "<file>")` of the citations the index knows, as character strings (write them to a workbook cell with `openxlsx::writeFormula()`; Excel limits a string in a formula to 255 characters, so longer paths are reported with a warning and are not linked). A citation the index does not know is listed in `unresolved_citations`; an index with the same file name twice uses the first and warns.

The question and answer text is returned as it is in the document. If you write it to a CSV or workbook, text that begins with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is read by spreadsheet programs as a formula.

See also

[docx_review_extract()], [package_deliverables()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
qa <- extract_docx_qa("investigator_questions.docx")
qa$citations

index <- data.frame(file = c("model_report.pdf"), path = c("reports/model_report.pdf"))
extract_docx_qa("investigator_questions.docx", index_data = index)$links
} # }
